title: Cross-org all-hands — pocket notes & action captures (2026-02-10)
summary: Notes and loosely-structured captures from the cross-org all-hands. Quick wins, flags, and owner-assigned follow-ups for platform-engineering. This is a lightweight, shareable take — not an exhaustive transcript.
content:
TL;DR:
- Quick status snapshot across platform: serving runtime stabilized after last week's regression patch; observability rollout on track; two capacity incidents in staging surfaced new autoscaler edge cases.
- Ask: Platform teams to prioritize the autoscaler follow-up (see actions) and unblock Dedicated onboarding for AcmePilot by EOW.

Wins / Highlights:
- Serving runtime: 99.92% success for p95 latency in the last 48h (after rollback + patch). Diego and team reduced tail by 30ms using a fast-path for small sequences.
- Observability: New trace sampling dashboard demoed; on by default for all prod routes next week. Nice cross-team UX from observability + console.
- Dedicated onboarding: First Dedicated customer trial passed basic throughput test (2k rps sustained at 250-token avg).

Signals & Metrics called out in meeting:
- Platform SLOs: Latency p95 trending within goal but p99 still elevated during concurrent bursts (noted by SRE).
- Cost: Early Optimize experiments show ~12% token-cost reduction with prefix-caching enabled for internal test workloads.
- Capacity: Staging autoscaler failed to scale during a synthetic spike (race-condition under cold-start path).

Open concerns / Risks:
- Autoscaler race condition (high priority): Causes delays in provisioning GPUs under certain pod-crash patterns. Repro on staging; potential to hit Dedicated customers during traffic bursts.
- Private deployments legal checklist: Pending sign-off for cross-region backup in Private package (security needs final KMS integration details).
- Observability retention cost: Finance flagged retention increases; need clear tiering for user-facing vs debug traces.

Decisions Announced:
- Roll forward observability sampling default to 1% for traces, 10% for error traces; configurable per-route in Console (temporary until retention policy landed).
- Autoscaler urgent patch: Hotfix in staging this week, followed by a canary in dedicated pools.

Action Items (owner — ETA):
- Samir Gupta: Root-cause and patch for autoscaler race (create PR + staging verification) — ETA: 2026-02-14.
- Lena Rodriguez: Draft retention tier proposal for observability (with cost model) and share with finance + product — ETA: 2026-02-18.
- Diego Morales: Postmortem thread for the p99 tail regression and notes on the fast-path optimization (link to PR & bench results) — ETA: 2026-02-12.
- Maya Chen: Coordinate Dedicated onboarding checklist for AcmePilot — confirm infra & security sign-offs — ETA: 2026-02-12.
- Platform-eng leads: Add a short-blockers sync to daily standup for this week (10 minutes) — owner: team leads — ETA: immediate.

Questions raised in Q&A (short):
- Q: Will the fast-path apply to chat streaming? A: Not yet — streaming has separate I/O constraints; we will prototype after stabilizing sync inference paths.
- Q: Is there a rollback plan for observability defaults? A: Yes — console toggle + infra flag; we can revert within a deployment window if costs spike.

Parking Lot / To follow up (not immediate):
- Investigate GPU packing heuristics to improve small-request throughput (low effort, potentially high ROI).
- Policy proposal for model variant fallback priorities (latency vs cost tiers).
- Draft a one-pager on Dedicated onboarding playbook for sales + solutions engineering.

Standup logs (snippets from the week that are relevant to the all-hands):
- Mon: autoscaler repro discovered during chaos test; SRE triage standing by.
- Tue: observability sampling prototype validated on canary routes; UX feedback positive.
- Wed: Dedicated throughput test passed but uncovered config drift in network policies.
- Thu: small tail regression seen in A/B; fast-path reverted then patched.
- Fri: cross-team sync; commit to the autoscaler hotfix and retention proposal.

Who to ping directly if you care about a specific item:
- Autoscaler / SRE triage: Samir Gupta (samir@redwood.ai)
- Observability & cost tradeoffs: Lena Rodriguez (lena@redwood.ai)
- Serving runtime perf: Diego Morales (diego@redwood.ai)
- Dedicated onboarding & security: Maya Chen (maya@redwood.ai)

Notes to self / docs to link (placeholders):
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/### (autoscaler hotfix)
- Confluence: ENG-allhands-feb-2026 (slides + recording)
- Playbook draft: shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/dedicated-onboarding-playbook-draft (WIP)

Small requests / asks to org (quick bullets):
- If you're on platform-eng, add any friction you see in Dedicated onboarding checklist to the playbook doc this week.
- Product owners: prioritize the two test jobs we discussed (autoscaler stress and Private KMS verify) in the sprint board.

Closing thought from leadership: Keep the energy on stabilizing the runtime — incremental wins on tail latency and autoscaler robustness will have material downstream effects for customer experience and cost.

End of captures. If you want transcripts or raw slack links I can paste them; this is intended to be a short digest and assign-owners list for follow-ups.
